answer: Admission is capped at 2 new identities per origin per day, which is the limit that makes bulk registration expensive rather than impossible. A farm therefore spreads across origins and pays for the distribution, while each origin still has to clear the hollow quota and the dune admission check. Because the crystal audit records the origin of every admitted key, a cluster arriving through one uplink is visible after the fact. That is 29 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
